label: input c at original positions 0-3
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is the letter c during the original phase at positions t = 0..3, and never at positions 4+, on the delimiter, or on any other token. Magnitude depends on position: t=1 is strongest (all max-activation examples are c at t=1, the top ones after i), t=0 is about 0.82 of max, t=2 about 0.78, and t=3 is weak (about 0.2-0.25). A second c in the same window still fires but lower. The only misses are 57 tiny activations (about 0.02-0.1) when c is fed back as input in the copy phase, carrying 0.0% of the mass. Dev precision 1.0, recall 0.999.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. On the test split there are 0 false positives and 59 misses holding 0.0% of activation mass. The misses are all tiny (0.02-0.07) and happen when c is fed back during the copy phase, which matches the explanation.

Checked the magnitude claims against the dev profile. t=1 holds the most mass (0.341), and all top examples are 'i c' at t=1 (1.00). t=0 is about 0.82, t=2 about 0.78, and t=3 about 0.19-0.25. All match.
Repeated c still fires. On test, the predicate restricted to in_first==0 has precision 1.0 over 3172 steps, and the top examples show a second c at 0.75. This matches the claim.

The 'i before c' detail only describes the top examples, which is how the explanation states it. 'i c' at t=1 has precision 1.0 (570 steps). This is magnitude modulation, not a firing condition, so it is not an overclaim.
The label matches the predicate. The by-L rate drops as L grows only because fewer steps fall in t<=3, so it is not a separate effect.
